_comment: VoiceKey config. Edit and restart. Key names use the `keyboard` library syntax: space, right ctrl, f13, etc. A USB foot pedal usually shows up as a normal key - press it in any text editor to see what it sends, then put that name here.

commands._comment: The escape phrase works like \n inside a string: everything before it is text, the words after it are an action.  "ship it zulu enter".  Pick a real word (invented words get mangled by transcription) that is RARE in normal speech. Avoid 'computer' - it is a shipping Alexa wake word and is documented to false-fire on words like 'pickle' and 'cotton'.
commands._comment2: Both ctrl keys work. The hook never suppresses, ignores a press made while alt/shift/win is held, and drops the capture as soon as any other key follows - so Ctrl+C is a copy, not a recording.
commands._comment3: Alt+Q stops it functioning but leaves it running; Ctrl+Alt+G starts it again. Quitting is the window's close button only. grid_hotkey is null on purpose - the grid is a voice command ("zulu grid"), and a hotkey for it collided with start/stop, which meant starting the app opened a grid. Set it to a key here if you want one.
commands._comment4: nudge_steps: the verb carries the distance, so choosing a magnitude costs no extra syllables. 'bump left' moves 8px, 'jump left' moves 500px. Size words multiply: 'skip left a lot' = 90px. An explicit count wins: 'jog left 120'.
commands._comment5: scroll takes an amount in wheel notches: 'scroll up 5', 'scroll down 12 clicks'. Bare 'scroll up' is 3. 'scroll up three times' is still a repeat, not an amount. Clamped to 100.

glow._comment: Screen-edge listening indicator. REINFORCEMENT ONLY - the earcons are the real signal, because an edge glow conveys nothing to a blind user and is the first thing cropped by a screen magnifier. animate:false gives a static border for anyone sensitive to peripheral motion; the indicator itself stays.
glow._comment2: soft:true uses a Windows layered window for TRUE per-pixel alpha - a real gradient falloff with rounded corners. If it fails for any reason it falls back automatically to the tkinter version (stipple dithering, looks like a screen door) and says so on the console. soft_thickness is the falloff depth in pixels: 45 is subtle, 80 is prominent.
glow._comment3: thickness/segments only affect the non-soft fallback path.
glow._comment4: fade_ms is the total fade in/out, driven by wall clock so a slow frame drops rather than stretching the fade. fade_interval_ms is how often it tries to repaint. Set fade_ms to 0 for no fade.

grid._comment: Fixed 5x5 = 25 cells. Each cell is 1/5 the width and 1/5 the height of the region, so a cell is the SAME SHAPE as the screen and the subdivision is self-similar - the zoom is always an exact fit, at any depth, on any display. 5 also keeps both axes single-digit, which is what makes selection two keystrokes with no Enter.
grid._comment2: settle_ms is the pause between moving the cursor and clicking; teardown_ms is how long the overlay gets to actually disappear first. If clicks land where the cursor already was, raise both.
